Administration and Management::Accountin.domain_definition: Tax advisory helps people and organisations understand and follow tax law. Tax advisors and compliance officers interpret legislation, inspect tax returns and study financial statements, while auditors, budget analysts and financial controllers check that accounts are accurate. Accounting firms, government revenue agencies and large companies employ most practitioners, and chartered qualifications are required to practise.

Corporate finance and investment banking deal with how companies raise, invest and manage money. Securities and mergers analysts study company performance and financial statements, while controllers, budget analysts and bank managers oversee funds and financial processes. Banks, investment firms and large corporations are the main employers.

Accounting is the recording, checking and reporting of an organisation's money. Accountants prepare and interpret financial statements, audit records, advise on tax, control budgets, and handle billing, payroll and back-office processing. They work in accounting firms, banks, government agencies and businesses of all sizes; in Nigeria the chartered route runs through bodies such as ICAN or ANAN.

Trading is the buying and selling of financial assets such as currencies, shares, commodities and energy. Traders deal on markets throughout the day, securities analysts study market trends and financial products, and investment managers and planners advise clients on funds and risk. Banks, investment firms and brokerages are the typical employers.

Investment analysis is the study of companies, markets and financial products to decide where money should be placed. Analysts examine businesses and market trends, investment managers run funds and portfolios, financial planners advise clients, and traders buy and sell shares, currencies and securities. Banks, investment firms, insurance companies and pension organisations are the main employers.

Economics studies how money, markets and government policy shape a society. Economists and researchers analyse statistics and market trends, while advisers and policy analysts guide decisions on tax, trade and economic development, often working closely with local representatives. Government ministries, research bodies and banks are common employers.

Insurance protects people and businesses against loss in exchange for regular payments. Underwriters assess risk and price cover, claims handlers and managers settle claims, brokers arrange policies for clients, fraud investigators check suspicious cases, and some specialists run pension schemes. Insurance companies and brokerages employ most of the profession.

Credit analysis is the work of judging whether borrowers can repay what they owe. Credit analysts and advisers examine financial statements, analyse loans and assess borrower risk, while credit managers and mortgage brokers arrange and oversee lending. Banks and other lending institutions employ most people in this field.

Keeping money safe and lending it out is the everyday business of banking and credit. Bank tellers and cashiers serve customers, credit analysts and advisers assess loans and mortgages, clerks handle settlements and foreign exchange records, and managers lead branches and credit unions. Banks, mortgage firms and credit unions are the natural workplaces.

Actuarial science uses mathematics and statistics to measure risk, mainly for insurance and pensions. Actuaries model how likely future events are and what cover should cost, underwriters and rating analysts assess individual risks, and claims handlers process what policyholders are owed. Most work in insurance companies, consulting firms and banks, and full actuaries qualify through professional fellowship examinations.

General management is the running of organisations and their departments. Managers direct budgets, finance, quality and facilities, consultants advise on strategy and business improvements, and senior executives and entrepreneurs lead whole organisations. Because every sector needs this work, managers are found in banks, factories, retailers, government agencies and non-profit organisations alike.

Public administration is the running of government and public institutions. Civil registration officers, urban planners and policy officers develop policy and public programmes, inspectors enforce customs, tax and safety rules, and senior officials and ambassadors lead ministries and diplomacy. Nearly all work in government ministries, agencies, local councils and embassies.

Project management is the planning and coordination of work so it finishes on time and within budget. Coordinators organise projects, procurement and office operations, senior managers lead programmes and departmental strategy, and analysts study processes to drive agile and lean improvements, often working with spreadsheets and business analysis. Construction firms, banks, government agencies and charities all need these skills.

Data science uses statistics and computer programming to draw useful conclusions from large collections of information. Some practitioners build data pipelines, artificial-intelligence models and software systems, while others model data with advanced mathematics, manage research information and write up findings in technical reports. Banks, telecoms companies, research bodies and government agencies all employ them.

Sales is the business of getting goods and services to buyers. Some practitioners purchase, broker and trade goods and commodities, others sell machinery, energy and technical products to businesses, manage key customer accounts, or serve shoppers on the shop floor, while directors set commercial strategy. Travel and tourism serves people on the move for holidays, business and leisure. Travel consultants plan trips and sell tickets, tour organisers and park guides lead visitors around attractions, and stewards look after passengers on flights, ships and trains. Basic Medical Sciences::Human Anatomy::D.domain_definition: Biomedical science studies living things, from microbes to the human body, mainly through laboratory work. Microbiologists, pharmacologists and physiologists research organisms, medicines and how bodies function, while technicians run laboratory tests and support biology and agricultural science. Hospitals, research institutes, universities and pharmaceutical companies employ them; medical laboratory scientists in Nigeria are licensed by MLSCN.

Biomedical engineering combines engineering with biology and medicine to design equipment and materials used in healthcare. Biomedical engineers and biomaterials scientists develop and test medical devices, while research and robotics engineers work on new technologies for the body. They are employed by hospitals, medical device manufacturers and research laboratories.

Neuroscience and cognitive science investigate the brain, thought and behaviour. One side of the field involves scientists studying how the brain and mind work; the other involves psychologists and psychotherapists who assess and treat mental and behavioural health. They work in hospitals, clinics, schools and universities.

Scientific research is the systematic study of the natural world through observation and experiment. Chemists, geologists and environmental scientists design studies and draft scientific papers, while technicians run laboratory tests, collect samples and support biology and agriculture research. Laboratories, research institutes, universities and government agencies are the usual workplaces.

Bioinformatics and computational biology use computers and data analysis to study living things, from microbes to human genes. Scientists such as geneticists, microbiologists and bioinformatics specialists run laboratory experiments, analyse biological data and write scientific papers. They generally work in research institutes, universities and hospitals.

Forensic science applies science and computing to the investigation of crime. Digital forensics experts and security specialists recover evidence from computers and respond to cyber attacks, laboratory technicians run biological analyses, detectives gather evidence, and pathologists examine medical evidence. Employers include police services, government agencies and security firms.

Medical laboratory technology is the testing of blood and other body samples to help doctors diagnose and treat illness. Phlebotomists collect blood, while technologists and technicians run clinical chemistry and molecular tests, classify blood types, maintain laboratory equipment and keep patient records. Hospitals, clinics and diagnostic laboratories employ most practitioners.

Higher education centres on teaching and leading colleges and universities, though the field also includes school-level teaching. Lecturers in subjects such as economics and medicine prepare lesson content, teach classes and assess students, while heads of institutions lead schools and faculties. Universities, colleges and other education institutions are the main employers.

They typically work in technology firms, banks, telecoms companies and government agencies.

Computing::Information Technology::D056.domain_definition: Blockchain work involves building software that records transactions on shared computer networks rather than in one central place. Smart contract and blockchain developers write the programs, security auditors and cryptography engineers test them for weaknesses, and architects and analysts design the wider systems. Software companies and financial organisations offer most roles.

Computing::Information Technology::D140.domain_definition: Robotics engineering designs machines that sense, move and act with little human control. Robotics, automation and controls engineers develop the mechanical parts, control systems and software that make robots work, relying on technical drawings and mathematics. They typically work for manufacturing companies, engineering firms and research organisations.

Computing::Information Technology::D009.domain_definition: Data science uses statistics and computer programming to draw useful conclusions from large collections of information. Some practitioners build data pipelines, artificial-intelligence models and software systems, while others model data with advanced mathematics, manage research information and write up findings in technical reports. Banks, telecoms companies, research bodies and government agencies all employ them.

Computing::Information Technology::D004.domain_definition: Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks and information from attack. Day to day, professionals administer security settings, investigate digital evidence after incidents, respond to cyber attacks, test defences as ethical hackers and manage security risks. They work in banks, telecoms companies, government agencies and any organisation that runs computer systems.

Computing::Information Technology::D002.domain_definition: Data engineering focuses on building the systems that collect, store and move an organisation's information. People in the field design data warehouses, connect databases to other software, write queries, and plan how information is structured so others can use it. Employers include banks, telecoms companies, technology firms and any large organisation that keeps substantial records.

Computing::Information Technology::D005.domain_definition: Cloud computing deals with running software and storing information on remote servers reached through the internet rather than on one office machine. Cloud architects plan these systems, engineers build and program them, administrators keep networks and data centres running, and specialists monitor security and compliance. Common employers are technology firms, banks, telecoms companies and data centres.

Computing::Information Technology::D008.domain_definition: Telecommunications is the engineering behind phone calls, internet connections and data networks. Engineers design radio-frequency and signal systems, planners work out how much network capacity is needed, technicians install and maintain equipment, and managers direct projects, budgets and technical teams. Telecoms companies and government agencies are the usual employers, and practising engineers in Nigeria register with COREN.

Computing::Information Technology::D003.domain_definition: Artificial intelligence covers building computer systems that learn from data to recognise images, understand language and make predictions. Machine learning engineers, data scientists and researchers write computer programs, apply statistics, run computer simulations and train models, then present their results visually. Typical workplaces include technology companies, research institutes, banks and universities.

Computing::Information Technology::D007.domain_definition: UI/UX design is about how websites and apps look, feel and respond when people use them. Sciences::Applied Geophysics::D072.domain_definition: Geospatial science involves measuring, mapping and studying the Earth's land, water and minerals. Surveyors take precise measurements of land, mines and seabeds for maps and property records, while geologists, hydrologists and oceanographers study rocks, groundwater and the sea using mathematics and geographic information systems. Typical employers include mining companies, construction firms and government agencies.

Sciences::Applied Geophysics::D022.domain_definition: Mining is the finding and extraction of minerals, oil and gas from the earth. Geologists and engineers explore and plan extraction sites, crews operate rigs, drills and underground machinery, managers run mines, quarries and production sites, and specialists survey ground, test metals and enforce safety rules. Mining companies, oil and gas producers and quarrying firms are the main employers.

Sciences::Applied Geophysics::D041.domain_definition: Scientific research is the systematic study of the natural world through observation and experiment. Chemists, geologists and environmental scientists design studies and draft scientific papers, while technicians run laboratory tests, collect samples and support biology and agriculture research. Laboratories, research institutes, universities and government agencies are the usual workplaces.

Sciences::Applied Geophysics::D020.domain_definition: Environmental engineering tackles pollution, waste and water quality. Technicians operate water, wastewater and waste treatment plants, engineers design solutions to pollution, climate and sustainability problems, and inspectors check that organisations comply with environmental, health and safety laws. Water utilities, waste management companies, mining firms and government agencies employ people in this field.

Sciences::Applied Geophysics::D059.domain_definition: Space technology concerns the design and operation of spacecraft and satellites. Aerospace, avionics and satellite systems engineers design and test flight hardware, propulsion engineers work on spacecraft engines, and mission operations engineers run missions once craft are in orbit, drawing heavily on physics. Space agencies, aerospace companies and research organisations are the usual employers.

Sciences::Applied Geophysics::D054.domain_definition: Finding petroleum underground and turning it into usable products is the focus of oil and gas work. Petroleum geologists and drilling engineers study rock and plan wells, operators run drills, pumps and refinery control rooms, and managers oversee offshore installations and production. Oil companies, refineries and servicing firms are the principal employers.

Sciences::Applied Geophysics::D144.domain_definition: Climate science and meteorology study the weather and the long-term behaviour of the atmosphere. Forecasters and meteorologists use instruments and specialised computer models to predict weather conditions, while climatologists, hydrologists and oceanographers analyse climate, water and ocean patterns. Typical employers are government weather agencies, aviation organisations and research institutes.

Sciences::Applied Geophysics::D156.domain_definition: Land surveying and cadastral mapping measure land and record its boundaries. Surveyors take precise measurements on building sites, mines and waterways, while cartographers, photogrammetrists and geographic information systems specialists turn those measurements into maps and digital records. Government agencies, construction firms and mining companies rely on their work.

Banks, investment firms and brokerages are the typical employers.

Investment analysis is the study of companies, markets and financial products to decide where money should be placed. Analysts examine businesses and market trends, investment managers run funds and portfolios, financial planners advise clients, and traders buy and sell shares, currencies and securities. Banks, investment firms, insurance companies and pension organisations are the main employers.

Recruitment and employment services match people to jobs. Recruitment consultants, talent acquisition specialists and employment agents advertise vacancies, interview and select candidates, follow labour legislation and keep candidate information confidential, while employer branding specialists present organisations attractively to job seekers. Recruitment agencies and company human resources departments are the typical employers.

Corporate finance and investment banking deal with how companies raise, invest and manage money. Securities and mergers analysts study company performance and financial statements, while controllers, budget analysts and bank managers oversee funds and financial processes. Banks, investment firms and large corporations are the main employers.

Public administration is the running of government and public institutions. Civil registration officers, urban planners and policy officers develop policy and public programmes, inspectors enforce customs, tax and safety rules, and senior officials and ambassadors lead ministries and diplomacy. Nearly all work in government ministries, agencies, local councils and embassies.

Legal practice covers the making, interpretation and application of law. Lawyers and legal consultants advise clients and argue cases, judges and court clerks run court processes and enforce decisions, and legal assistants compile documents and carry out legal research. Typical workplaces include law firms, courts, companies and government agencies.

Veterinary Medicine::Veterinary Medicine.domain_definition: Veterinary science is the study and treatment of animal health and welfare. Veterinarians diagnose, treat and rehabilitate sick or injured animals, veterinary nurses assist with care and breeding procedures, and others provide animal therapy or study behaviour and nutrition. Practitioners work in veterinary clinics, on farms and for government agencies, and must register with the Veterinary Council of Nigeria to practise.

Animal care and grooming is the everyday looking after of animals, from feeding and cleaning to training and grooming. Attendants and kennel workers care for animals in shelters and boarding facilities, trainers teach dogs and horses, breeders raise animals, and groomers keep coats healthy and tidy. Kennels, stables, zoos and grooming salons are the typical workplaces.

Livestock, poultry and dairy work is the rearing of animals for food and other products. Farmers and breeders raise cattle, poultry, sheep, horses and bees and run dairy farms, while livestock workers feed, handle and groom animals under animal-welfare rules. Work is based on farms, ranches and dairies.

Microbiologists, pharmacologists and physiologists research organisms, medicines and how bodies function, while technicians run laboratory tests and support biology and agricultural science. Hospitals, research institutes, universities and pharmaceutical companies employ them; medical laboratory scientists in Nigeria are licensed by MLSCN.

Veterinary Medicine::Veterinary Medicine.domain_definition: Biomedical engineering combines engineering with biology and medicine to design equipment and materials used in healthcare. Biomedical engineers and biomaterials scientists develop and test medical devices, while research and robotics engineers work on new technologies for the body. They are employed by hospitals, medical device manufacturers and research laboratories.

Scientific research is the systematic study of the natural world through observation and experiment. Chemists, geologists and environmental scientists design studies and draft scientific papers, while technicians run laboratory tests, collect samples and support biology and agriculture research. Laboratories, research institutes, universities and government agencies are the usual workplaces.

Public health protects the health of whole communities rather than one patient at a time. Inspectors enforce food, workplace and community health standards, officers and physicians coordinate emergency responses and prevention work, and scientists track diseases and analyse health statistics. Government agencies, hospitals and international health organisations are typical employers.

From crops to livestock, agricultural science combines farming practice with the study of plants, animals and the environment. Crop production managers, breeders and shepherds grow crops and raise animals, researchers study genetics, biology and aquaculture, and technicians supervise farm and fish sites. Farms, research institutes, agribusinesses and government agricultural agencies offer most positions.
